about: How a secret setting (DESIGN 5.27) is kept in the Windows Credential Manager, alike on every stack, so an application built on another stack finds what this one kept. A generic credential whose target is the program's name, a colon and the setting's name, whose user is the setting's name, whose blob is the value's UTF-8 bytes (`blob`, in hex), and whose persistence is the local machine's (`persist`: CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE, 2), as go-keyring writes it. Not enterprise persistence (3, keyring-rs's own), which roams with the person's account: a secret forgotten on this machine could come back from it.
programs_about: The program's name, which every stack gives the runtime for its settings folder (DESIGN 5.17) and its secrets, desktop and command-line program alike: the project's name in snake case (`clarity_gen::settings_program`). One form everywhere, all lower case: the Credential Manager reads a target whatever its case but writes one apart for each case, so `Shop:shopDb` and `shop:shopDb` would be two secrets that read as one.
